description.narrative: The Irish Bursary for Karamoja implemented by Straight Talk Foundation aims to increase access to quality education and skilling for Karamoja children and youth, with a focus on inclusion and gender equality. In 2024, the programme will support a total of 1,424 scholars (1,329 scholars at secondary level and 95 at tertiary level). Indirect beneficiaries Include key stakeholders such as parents, teachers/ mentors, opinion/ religious leaders, likeminded organizations, school management and the community in Karamoja. Results targeted:1. Disadvantaged but bright young people from the 9 districts of Karamoja are enabled to access post-primary and post-secondary education.2. School fees, basic education requirements and incentives provided to all scholars at all levels-post primary and secondary education. 3. Change in attitudes, behaviours and practice among bursary holders and their parents/ guardians towards a more positive view of education.4. A strengthened and functional Bursary alumni network and other programme engagements.Learners with special needs are given priority as a target group. STF’s Bursary Operational Manual commits to having applicants with special needs on the programme by assessing the level of disability, documenting and exploring how the child with high or multiple disabilities can be supported.The selection tool clearly provides for an applicant is an extremely vulnerable young person living with disability (it is the intention of the bursary program to include people with disability on the program), siblings, elderly grandparents. Much as the Bursery programme incorporates explicit mechanisms to promote inclusion of children with disabilities such as in selection, risk mitigation and refferal to ensure that learners with special needs are given priority as a target group, and that the STF’s Bursary Operational Manual futher commits to having applicants with special needs on the programme by assessing the level of disability, documenting and exploring how the child with high or multiple disabilities can be supported.
